skill.name: when-auditing-security-use-security-analyzer
skill.description: Run a multi-phase security audit workflow for codebases, including static checks, dependency review, secret detection, dynamic testing guidance, and OWASP reporting.
skill.summary: Coordinates static analysis, dependency auditing, secret scanning, dynamic checks, and OWASP review for application security work.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: I confirmed operational risks around broad filesystem scans, predictable temporary artifacts, secret finding retention, and active localhost testing. Many static hits are false positives from vulnerability examples, code fences, regex patterns, and safe scanner logic rather than malicious code. No prompt-injection attempt or external exfiltration endpoint was found.

remediation.issue: Sensitive scan artifacts can be written to predictable temporary paths and shared memory.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp directories with 0700 permissions, redact secret values before storage, and delete temporary artifacts after reporting.

remediation.issue: The scan path can cover more files than intended.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit scan paths, reject root and home directories by default, and document safe project-scoped usage.

remediation.issue: Dynamic testing examples send offensive payloads to local services.
remediation.suggestion: Run active tests only against isolated test environments, make target URLs explicit, and require confirmation before high-volume checks.

remediation.issue: Vulnerable examples and executable snippets are mixed in the same documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Clearly separate illustrative vulnerable code from runnable workflow commands to reduce scanner noise and misuse risk.

content.user_title: Audit Code Security With Analyzer Workflows
content.value_statement: Security reviews require repeatable checks across code, dependencies, secrets, runtime behavior, and compliance. This skill organizes those checks into a phased workflow with reports and remediation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Defines a five-phase audit flow for static analysis, dynamic testing, dependency audit, secrets detection, and OWASP review.
Provides shell and Claude Flow examples for running audits, storing findings, and generating reports.
Documents grep, npm audit, jq, curl, and license-checker based checks for JavaScript projects.
Includes a slash command script with scan type, path, severity, output format, quick mode, and strict mode options.
Explains validation gates and exit codes for critical, high, configuration, and incomplete scan outcomes.
limitations: Most detections are pattern based and can produce false positives or miss complex vulnerabilities.
Dynamic checks mainly target a local application on port 3000 and require the service to be running.
The workflow focuses on JavaScript and npm ecosystems and may not cover other stacks well.
Generated reports may include sensitive findings, so storage and sharing need access controls.

best_practices: Run scans in an isolated test environment with explicit target paths and non-production credentials.
Review findings manually before blocking a release because pattern-based checks can create false positives.
Protect generated reports because they can contain source paths, dependency details, and secret indicators.
anti_patterns: Do not run active dynamic tests against production services without written authorization.
Do not store raw secret findings in shared folders, logs, tickets, or chat systems.
Do not treat a clean pattern scan as proof that the application is secure.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It organizes static analysis, dynamic testing guidance, dependency review, secret detection, and OWASP compliance checks.

faq.question: Does it replace a professional penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure checks and reports, but expert review is still needed for high assurance.

faq.question: Which projects fit best?
faq.answer: It fits JavaScript and npm projects best because many examples use grep, npm audit, jq, curl, and Node tooling.

faq.question: Can it produce false positives?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow uses pattern matching, so reviewers should confirm each finding before making release decisions.

faq.question: Does it access network resources?
faq.answer: The documented dynamic checks target localhost, and dependency tooling may contact package audit services when run.

faq.question: How should reports be handled?
faq.answer: Treat reports as sensitive because they may include vulnerability details, source paths, and secret indicators.
